chunks: Khaybari ibn Ali, al-Tahhan (the miller), Kufan. Weak in hadith, Ghali in madhhab. He was a companion of Yunus ibn Zibyan, and narrated a lot from him. He has a book from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). His hadith are not regarded.

key_terms.الطَّحَّانُ: al-Tahhan, meaning the miller, a kunya or descriptor
key_terms.خَيْبَرِيُّ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ: Khaybari ibn Ali, the narrator's name
key_terms.ضَعِيفُ الْحَدِيثِ: Weak in hadith, indicating lower reliability in narration
key_terms.غَالِي الْمَذْهَبِ: Ghali in madhhab, meaning he exaggerated in religious belief
key_terms.لَا يُلْتَفَتُ إِلَى حَدِيثِهِ: His hadith are not regarded/relied upon
key_terms.يُونُسَ بْنَ ظِبْيَانَ: Yunus ibn Zibyan, a companion he associated with

ai.seo_question: Who is Khaybari ibn Ali and what is his status in Shia hadith sciences?
ai.summary: This entry from Kitab al-Du'afa describes the narrator Khaybari ibn Ali, noting his weakness in hadith transmission and his tendency to be Ghali (exaggerating in belief). It mentions his association with Yunus ibn Zibyan and states that his narrations are generally not relied upon.
